mainTopic: סנחריב's march on ירושלים and its downfall, the story of דוד and ישבי בנוב, and the three people for whom the land shrank.
overview: The גמרא finishes reading the verses in ישעיהו 10 about סנחריב's march on ירושלים. 'עניה ענתות' hints that ירמיהו of ענתות will prophesy about נבוכדנצר. רבי יוחנן explains that ארי and ליש are both names for a lion, and the count of ten stops still works because עברו and מעברה are two places. רב הונא teaches that 'עוד היום בנב' means only one day was left of the punishment for the sin of נוב. סנחריב rushes to ירושלים, mocks the small city, and puts off the attack until morning, and that night an angel destroys his army. רב פפא sums it up: a judgment left overnight is cancelled. The theme of נוב then leads to the story of ישבי בנוב. He was sent to punish דוד for נוב, and אבישי rescued דוד through a holy שם and prayer. Finally, a ברייתא lists three people for whom the land shrank, and the list of sources for יעקב אבינו continues on the next amud.

steps.title: עניה ענתות hints at ירמיהו's prophecy
steps.stepSummary: The words 'עניה ענתות' are explained as a hint that ירמיהו, a כהן from ענתות, will one day prophesy about נבוכדנצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Poor Anathoth': ירמיהו son of חלקיה will one day prophesy about him from ענתות, as the פסוק says, 'The words of ירמיהו son of חלקיהו, of the כהנים who were in ענתות in the land of בנימין.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the phrase 'עניה ענתות' in ישעיהו. It says this phrase points to ירמיהו, who came from ענתות and would later prophesy about נבוכדנצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ענתות is not read here as just one more stop on סנחריב's march. Instead it is read as a hint to the town of ירמיהו. The proof that ירמיהו came from ענתות is the very first פסוק of his book.

keyTerms.meaning: The town of the כהנים in the land of בנימין where ירמיהו came from

phrases.english: "Poor Anathoth":
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 10:30

phrases.english: Jeremiah son of Hilkiah is destined
to prophesy about it from Anathoth,
phrases.notes: "About it" means about the coming of נבוכדנצר, the 'lion' the גמרא was just talking about.

phrases.english: as it is written:
"The words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah,
of the priests who were in Anathoth
in the land of Benjamin."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 1:1

steps.triggerLanguage: עניה ענתות עתיד ירמיה בן חלקיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier verse-by-verse reading of ישעיהו 10, where the 'lion' was read as a hint to נבוכדנצר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'עניה ענתות' hints that ירמיהו of ענתות will prophesy about נבוכדנצר.

steps.title: ירמיהו says 'ארי' but ישעיהו says 'ליש'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the two נביאים use different words for the lion, so the link between them seems weak.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they really the same? There, ירמיהו calls him 'ארי', and here, ישעיהו says 'ליש'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the link it just made between ישעיהו and ירמיהו. The two נביאים use different words for the lion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reading in step 1 depends on both נביאים talking about the same 'lion', נבוכדנצר. If ירמיהו uses 'ארי' and ישעיהו uses 'ליש', perhaps they are not talking about the same thing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they comparable? A challenge that two cases are not alike

phrases.english: Are they comparable?
There it is "ari," here it is "laish"!

steps.triggerLanguage: מי דמי התם ארי הכא ליש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the link between the verses made in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ישעיהו's 'ליש' and ירמיהו's lion refer to the same נבוכדנצר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Different words suggest different subjects, so the comparison between the two verses fails.

steps.title: The lion has six names
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that 'ארי' and 'ליש' are both names for a lion, so the two נביאים can be talking about the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The lion has six names: ארי, כפיר, לביא, ליש, שחל, שחץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a teaching of רבי יוחנן. 'ארי' and 'ליש' are just two of the six names for a lion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The change in wording does not mean the subject changed. Both words mean 'lion', so ישעיהו and ירמיהו can both be describing נבוכדנצר.

keyTerms.meaning: Two more names for a lion

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The lion has six names,
and these are they: ari, kefir, lavi,
layish, shachal, shachatz.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי יוחנן ששה שמות יש לארי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the two different words mean the same thing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ארי' and 'ליש' are different words, so the verses are about different things.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are names for a lion, so both verses refer to נבוכדנצר.
steps.whatToRemember: The lion has six names in לשון הקודש. That is why ישעיהו's 'ליש' and ירמיהו's 'ארי' can describe the same נבוכדנצר.

steps.title: Then there are too few stops on the march
steps.stepSummary: If these words are about נבוכדנצר and not about the places on סנחריב's march, the list of places is short of ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there are too few of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem. If these words are hints about נבוכדנצר and not names of places, then the count of סנחריב's stops comes out too low.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא counted ten stops on סנחריב's march in these פסוקים. Taking some of the words away as hints to נבוכדנצר leaves fewer than ten places.

keyTerms.meaning: They are too few, they come out short

phrases.english: If so, they are too few!
phrases.notes: 'They' are the ten stops on סנחריב's march. If these words aren't places, the list falls short of ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer in step 3 but shows that the reading causes a new problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading these words as hints to נבוכדנצר and not as places.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים are supposed to list ten stops. Removing some of them leaves the count short.

steps.title: עברו and מעברה are two places
steps.stepSummary: The count is saved by treating 'עברו מעברה' as two separate places.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'עברו מעברה' are two places.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'עברו מעברה' is not one place but two. This fills the gap in the count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By splitting one phrase into two place names, the list still reaches ten stops. This works even though some of the words were read as hints to נבוכדנצר.

keyTerms.meaning: Words from ישעיהו 10:29, read here as two place names

phrases.english: "Averu Mabara"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 10:29

phrases.english: are two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recounting the places in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'עברו מעברה' is one place, so the list is short.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'עברו' and 'מעברה' are two places, so the count of ten is complete.

steps.title: What does 'This very day at נוב' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the words 'עוד היום בנב לעמוד' mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'This very day he shall halt at נוב'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק and asks what 'today at נוב' means. This sets up רב הונא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'עוד היום', 'still today', sound like there was something special about that day. The גמרא wants to know why that day mattered.

keyTerms.meaning: נוב, the city of the כהנים

phrases.english: What is "This very day
he shall halt at Nov"?
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 10:32

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase in ישעיהו 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק stresses 'today' at נוב.

steps.title: The last day of punishment for the sin of נוב
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that this was the last day left of the punishment for the sin of נוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: That day was what was left of the punishment for the sin of נוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question. That day was the final day the Jewish people were still being punished for the sin of נוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עוד היום' means 'only today is left'. After this day, the punishment for נוב would end and סנחריב would lose his chance.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
That day was what remained
from the sin of Nov.
phrases.notes: See שמואל א פרק כב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב הונא אותו היום נשתייר מעונה של נוב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: That day was the last day of punishment for the sin of נוב.

steps.title: The astrologers' warning and the rushed march
steps.stepSummary: The astrologers tell סנחריב he can win only if he attacks now, so he covers a ten-day road in one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The astrologers said to him: If you go now, you will beat them. If not, you will not beat them. So a road that takes ten days to walk, he walked in one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the story. סנחריב is told that today is his only chance, so he rushes to ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to רב הונא's point that only one day of punishment was left. סנחריב's astrologers sensed the deadline, which is why he raced a ten-day road in a single day.

phrases.english: The astrologers said to him:
If you go now, you will overcome it,
phrases.notes: "It" means ירושלים and the Jewish people in it.

phrases.english: and if not, you will not overcome it.
A road that needs to be walked in ten days,
he walked in one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמרי ליה כלדאי אי אזלת האידנא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story that builds on רב הונא's 'last day' explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Told he could win only that day, סנחריב rushed a ten-day road in one day.

steps.title: סנחריב climbs up and sees ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: At ירושלים, mats are piled up so סנחריב can sit above the wall and see the whole city, and it looks small to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they reached ירושלים, they piled up mats for him until he climbed up and sat above the wall and could see all of ירושלים. When he saw it, it looked small in his eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. סנחריב gets a high view of ירושלים and is not impressed by what he sees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeing the whole city at once made it look small. This sets up his proud and mocking speech in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It became small in his eyes

phrases.english: When they reached Jerusalem,
they threw down mats for him,
phrases.notes: They piled the mats up high, like a tower he could climb.

phrases.english: until he went up and sat above the wall,
so that he saw all of Jerusalem.
When he saw it, it became small in his eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: כי מטו לירושלם שדו ליה ביסתרקי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of סנחריב's arrival.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From above the wall, ירושלים looked small to סנחריב.

steps.title: סנחריב mocks the city and waves at the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: סנחריב scornfully asks whether this small, weak city is what he gathered all his armies for, and he shakes his head and waves his hand at the הר הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Is this the city of ירושלים, for which I stirred up all my armies and conquered all the countries? Isn't it smaller and weaker than all the cities of the nations that I conquered with my strength? He stood up, shook his head, and waved his hand back and forth at the הר הבית in ציון and at the עזרה in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: סנחריב mocks ירושלים as tiny and weak. He makes a gesture of contempt toward the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His speech shows his arrogance: he thinks his own strength won all his battles. His waving hand matches the פסוק's picture of him shaking his hand at הר ציון.

keyTerms.meaning: The courtyard of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: He said:
Is this not the city of Jerusalem
for which I stirred up all my armies,
and for which I conquered all the countries?
Is it not smaller and weaker
than all the cities of the nations
that I conquered with the strength of my hands?
He went up, stood, and shook his head,
waving his hand back and forth
at the Temple Mount that is in Zion
and at the courtyard that is in Jerusalem.
phrases.notes: This matches the end of ישעיהו 10:32: 'he shakes his hand at the mount of the daughter of ציון.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר הלא דא היא קרתא דירושלם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: after seeing the city, סנחריב mocks it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סנחריב scorned ירושלים as small and weak and waved his hand at the בית המקדש.
steps.whatToRemember: סנחריב rushed to ירושלים on the last day of the punishment for נוב. Then he looked down on the city and mocked the בית המקדש.

steps.title: The officers want to attack now, but סנחריב says wait until tomorrow
steps.stepSummary: סנחריב's officers want to attack ירושלים right away. He tells them they are tired and should finish the job tomorrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: His officers said: Let's attack it now. He said to them: You are tired. Tomorrow each of you will bring me a small piece of the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of סנחריב continues. His officers want to attack immediately, but he decides to wait one more day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the turning point of the story. Step 7 said that this was the very last day of the punishment for נוב. By putting off the attack until tomorrow, סנחריב throws away his only chance to win.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us attack it (literally, 'throw a hand at it')
You are weary or worn out
A small piece, the size of a letter's seal

phrases.english: They said: Let us attack it now.
phrases.notes: Literally 'let us throw a hand at it.' His officers are the ones speaking.

phrases.english: He said to them: You are weary.

phrases.aramaic: לִמְחַר אַיְיתוֹ לִי כֹּל חַד וְחַד מִינַּיְיכוּ
phrases.english: Tomorrow, each and every one of you will bring me
a seal-sized piece from it.
phrases.notes: He means a small piece of the wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the scene at the wall from Step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סנחריב postpones the attack by one night.

steps.title: That night an angel destroys the Assyrian army
steps.stepSummary: Right away, that same night, an angel of ה׳ kills 185,000 soldiers in the camp of אשור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately: 'And that night the angel of ה׳ went out and struck 185,000 in the camp of אשור, and in the morning they were all dead bodies.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק showing what happened because סנחריב waited: his army was wiped out that same night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מיד ('immediately') links the delay directly to the disaster. Once the last day of the punishment for נוב was over, ירושלים was protected again.

phrases.english: Immediately: "And it came to pass on that night
that the angel of the Lord went out
and struck in the camp of Assyria
one hundred eighty-five thousand;
and they arose in the morning,
and behold, they were all dead corpses."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 19:35

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what happened because of the delay in Step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Assyrian army is destroyed the night after the last day of the punishment ends.

steps.title: רב פפא: a judgment left overnight is cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא sums up the story with a popular saying: if a judgment waits overnight, it is cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is what people say: a judgment that waits overnight is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא closes the סנחריב story by tying it to a well-known saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree against ירושלים was good for one day only. Because סנחריב did not act on that day, the decree ran out and could no longer be carried out.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (introduces a popular saying)

steps.whatToRemember: The decree against ירושלים lasted only until the end of the last day. סנחריב waited one night too long, so the decree ran out and his army was destroyed.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This is what people say:
A judgment that stays overnight is a judgment cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the outcome in Step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A decree that is not carried out in its time is cancelled.

steps.title: A new פסוק about ישבי בנוב, who tried to kill דוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק about a giant named ישבי בנוב, who planned to kill דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And ישבי בנוב, one of the children of the giant, whose spear weighed three hundred shekels of copper, and who was dressed in new armor, planned to kill דוד.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new story that is also connected to נוב. Here it is setting up the next move by quoting the פסוק it is about to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name in the פסוק contains the word נוב. That is the link to the earlier story, and the גמרא is about to explain what the name means.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of a Philistine giant

phrases.english: "And Yishbi Benov, who was of the children of the giant,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִשְׁקַל קֵינוֹ שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת מִשְׁקַל נְחֹשֶׁת
phrases.english: and the weight of whose spear was three hundred shekels of copper,
and he was girded with new armor,
and he planned to strike David."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 21:16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story, linked to the earlier one through the theme of נוב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The base פסוק for the story of ישבי בנוב.

steps.title: What does the name ישבי בנוב mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the strange name ישבי בנוב is hinting at.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'ישבי בנוב'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question about the meaning of the name in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name sounds unusual, so the גמרא suspects it carries a hidden message. The answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: What is "and Yishbi Benov"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the name in the פסוק quoted in Step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning behind the name ישבי בנוב

steps.title: A man who came because of נוב
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, explains that the name means 'a man who came because of what happened at נוב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: It means a man who came because of the matters of נוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 15 by reading the name as a hint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישבי is read like 'איש בא', a man who came, and בנוב is read as 'because of נוב'. So this giant was sent to punish דוד for his part in the disaster at נוב.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A man who came over the matters of Nov.
phrases.notes: The name ישבי sounds like 'איש בא', 'a man came.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אִישׁ שֶׁבָּא עַל עִסְקֵי נוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ישבי בנוב means a man who came to punish דוד over נוב.

steps.title: ה׳ holds דוד responsible for three tragedies
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ tells דוד that because of him, נוב was destroyed, דואג האדומי was lost, and שאול and his three sons were killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: ה׳ said to דוד: How long will this sin stay hidden in your hand? Because of you, נוב, the city of the כהנים, was killed; because of you, דואג האדומי was driven away; and because of you, שאול and his three sons were killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the 'matters of נוב' were: ה׳ lists three terrible results that came about because of דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד did not kill anyone at נוב himself. But his visit there set off a chain of events, so he is held responsible for the results. This explains why a punisher was sent after him.

keyTerms.meaning: Hidden in your hand, meaning not yet punished

steps.confusionAlert: דוד did not kill the people of נוב. שאול and דואג did. דוד is blamed because his actions caused the chain of events that led there.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְדָוִד:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to David:

phrases.aramaic: עַד מָתַי יִהְיֶה עָוֹן זֶה טָמוּן בְּיָדְךָ?
phrases.english: Until when will this sin be hidden in your hand?

phrases.aramaic: עַל יָדְךָ נֶהֶרְגָה נוֹב עִיר הַכֹּהֲנִים,
phrases.english: Through you, Nov, the city of the priests, was killed,
and through you, Doeg the Edomite was banished,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל יָדְךָ נֶהֶרְגוּ שָׁאוּל וּשְׁלֹשֶׁת בָּנָיו.
phrases.english: and through you, Saul and his three sons were killed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְדָוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the 'matters of נוב' mentioned in Step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד is held responsible for the chain of tragedies that started at נוב.

steps.title: דוד chooses to be handed to an enemy rather than lose his descendants
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ lets דוד choose: his descendants will end, or he will be handed over to an enemy. דוד chooses the enemy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you prefer that your descendants come to an end, or that you be handed over to an enemy? He said before Him: Master of the World, it is better that I be handed over to an enemy and my descendants not end.
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ offers דוד a choice of punishment, and דוד picks being handed to an enemy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This choice sets up the next part of the story. Because דוד chose to be handed to an enemy, he will now be led straight into the hands of ישבי בנוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Your descendants will come to an end
You will be handed over to an enemy

phrases.english: Do you want your descendants to come to an end,
or that you be handed over to an enemy?
He said before Him: Master of the World,
it is better that I be handed over to an enemy
and that my descendants not come to an end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the punishment that follows from the accusation in Step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד chooses to be handed to an enemy.

steps.title: The שטן disguised as a deer lures דוד into Philistine land
steps.stepSummary: While דוד is hunting, the שטן appears as a deer and leads him into the land of the פלשתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day דוד went out to hunt with falcons. The שטן came and appeared to him as a deer. He shot an arrow at it and did not reach it. It pulled him along until it brought him to the land of the פלשתים.
steps.whatsHappening: The punishment begins. The שטן tricks דוד and draws him into enemy territory.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is how דוד ends up 'handed to an enemy', just as he chose. His arrow keeps missing, so he keeps chasing until he is deep in Philistine land.

phrases.english: One day he went out to hunt with falcons,
Satan came and appeared to him as a deer.
He shot an arrow at it, and it did not reach it.
It drew him along until it brought him to the land of the Philistines.
phrases.notes: The 'deer', which is really the שטן, keeps leading דוד on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins carrying out the punishment דוד chose in Step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד is lured into enemy territory.

steps.title: ישבי בנוב captures דוד and tries to crush him
steps.stepSummary: ישבי בנוב recognizes דוד as the one who killed his brother גלית. He ties him up and throws him under an olive press.
steps.simpleTranslation: When ישבי בנוב saw him, he said: This is the one who killed גלית my brother. He tied him up, bent him over, set him down, and threw him under an olive press.
steps.whatsHappening: The enemy catches דוד and tries to kill him by crushing him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now ישבי בנוב, the 'man who came because of נוב', has דוד in his power. He also has a personal reason to want revenge: גלית was his brother.

phrases.english: When Yishbi Benov saw him, he said:
This is the one who killed Goliath, my brother.
He tied him up, bent him over, set him down,
and threw him under an olive press.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after דוד arrives in Philistine land
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישבי בנוב captures דוד and tries to crush him.

steps.title: A miracle: the ground sinks under דוד
steps.stepSummary: A miracle happens: the ground sinks beneath דוד so the press cannot crush him. The גמרא links this to a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A miracle was done for him: the ground sank down beneath him. This is what is written: 'You widened my steps beneath me, and my ankles did not slip.'
steps.whatsHappening: דוד is saved by a miracle, and the גמרא shows that a פסוק hints at it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the ground went down under him, the weight of the press did not crush דוד. The פסוק's words 'You widened my steps beneath me' are read as describing exactly this.

phrases.english: A miracle was done for him:
the ground sank down beneath him.
This is what is written:
"You have enlarged my steps beneath me, and my ankles did not slip."
phrases.notes: תהלים 18:37

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how דוד survives the attack in Step 20
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד is saved by a miracle, hinted at in a פסוק in תהלים.

steps.title: אבישי sees a sign that דוד is in trouble
steps.stepSummary: On ערב שבת, אבישי בן צרויה sees the water turn to bloodstains, or a dove flutters before him. He concludes that דוד is in distress.
steps.simpleTranslation: That day was ערב שבת toward evening. אבישי was washing his hair with four jugs of water and saw bloodstains. Some say a dove came and fluttered in front of him. He said: כנסת ישראל is compared to a dove, so דוד, the king of Israel, must be in trouble.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves to a new person, אבישי בן צרויה, who gets a sign from heaven that דוד is in danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions of the sign: blood in the wash water, or a dove fluttering in front of him. In the dove version, אבישי uses a פסוק that compares כנסת ישראל to a dove. Since the king stands for the whole nation, he reads the sign as a message about דוד.

keyTerms.meaning: דוד's nephew and one of his top warriors
some say (a second version of the story)
the Jewish people as a whole

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא יוֹמָא אַפַּנְיָא דְּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא הֲוָה.
phrases.english: That day was toward evening on Shabbat eve.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבִישַׁי בֶּן צְרוּיָה הֲוָה קָא חָיֵיף רֵישֵׁיהּ
phrases.english: Avishai ben Tzeruyah was washing his head
with four jugs of water.
He saw them as stains of blood.
phrases.notes: He means the water looked to him like bloodstains.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
A dove came and fluttered in front of him.
He said: The community of Israel is compared to a dove,
as it is said: "The wings of a dove covered with silver."
phrases.notes: תהלים 68:14

phrases.english: Learn from this that David, king of Israel,
is in distress.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא יוֹמָא אַפַּנְיָא דְּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבְּתָא הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: דוד is stuck under the olive press. The story now turns to the person who will rescue him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sign from heaven, explained through a פסוק about a dove, shows אבישי that דוד is in distress.

steps.title: May אבישי use the king's animal in an emergency?
steps.stepSummary: אבישי can't find דוד at home. He wants to use דוד's animal, but a משנה forbids using the king's things, so he asks what the rule is in a time of danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came to דוד's house and did not find him. He said: We learned that no one may ride the king's horse, sit on his throne, or use his scepter. What is the rule in a time of danger? He went and asked in the בית מדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: אבישי stops to ask a halachic question before using the king's mule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (earlier in this מסכתא) teaches that the king's personal things are off-limits to everyone else. אבישי asks whether that rule still holds when the king's life is at risk. Even in a rush, he will not act until he knows the halacha.

keyTerms.meaning: the בית מדרש, the study hall

steps.confusionAlert: The horse, throne, and scepter belong to the king. The question is whether someone else may use the king's things to save him.

phrases.english: He came to his house and did not find him.
He said: We learned:
One may not ride on his horse
and one may not sit on his throne
and one may not use his scepter.
In a time of danger, what is the rule?
He came and asked in the study hall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After learning that דוד is in danger, אבישי needs a way to reach him and faces a halachic question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ban on using the king's horse, throne, and scepter still apply when the king is in danger?

steps.title: In danger, it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The בית מדרש answers that in a time of danger, using the king's things is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: In a time of danger, it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The בית מדרש answers אבישי's question: in danger, he may use the king's things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule protecting the king's honor gives way when the king's life is at stake. This clears the way for אבישי to ride the king's mule in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: it is fine, it is permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the honor rules for a king do not stand in the way of saving him.

phrases.english: They said to him:
In a time of danger, it is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: בִּשְׁעַת הַסַּכָּנָה שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In a time of danger, one may use the king's things.

steps.title: אבישי's miraculous ride and the death of ערפה
steps.stepSummary: אבישי rides דוד's mule, and the land miraculously shortens for him. On the way, ערפה, the mother of ישבי בנוב, tries to kill him with her spindle, and he kills her with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He rode his mule and set out. The land shrank for him. As he traveled, he saw ערפה, the mother of ישבי בנוב, spinning. When she saw him, she pulled off her spindle and threw it at him to kill him. She said: Young man, bring me the spindle! He threw it at the top of her head and killed her.
steps.whatsHappening: With permission granted, אבישי rushes to דוד. On the way he meets and kills the mother of ישבי בנוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Riding the king's mule shows that אבישי acted on the ruling of the בית מדרש. The land shrinking is a miracle that brings him there fast. ערפה's attack fails, and her own spindle becomes the weapon that kills her.

keyTerms.meaning: the land 'jumped' for him; the trip miraculously shrank
ערפה, here named as the mother of ישבי בנוב

phrases.english: He rode his mule, and got up and went.
phrases.notes: 'His mule' is דוד's mule, the king's animal he just got permission to use.

phrases.english: The land jumped for him.
phrases.notes: Literally 'jumped': the road shrank by a miracle, so he got there very fast.

phrases.english: As he was traveling,
he saw Orpah his mother, who was spinning.
phrases.notes: 'His mother' means the mother of ישבי בנוב.

phrases.english: When she saw him, she pulled off her spindle,
threw it at him, intending to kill him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: עֻלֵם, אַיְיתִי לִי פְּלַךְ!
phrases.english: She said to him: Young man, bring me the spindle!
He threw it at the top of her head and killed her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Acting on the permission from step 24, אבישי rides the king's mule toward דוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבישי reaches the land of the פלשתים by a miracle and kills ערפה when she tries to kill him.

steps.title: אבישי holds דוד in mid-air with a holy שם
steps.stepSummary: ישבי בנוב sees אבישי and knows two warriors can kill him. He throws דוד into the air over his upright spear, but אבישי says a holy שם and holds דוד up between heaven and earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: When ישבי בנוב saw him, he said: Now there are two, and they will kill me. He threw דוד up high and stuck his spear in the ground, saying: Let him fall on it and die. אבישי said a holy שם and held דוד in place between heaven and earth.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the high point of the rescue. ישבי בנוב tries to kill דוד on his spear, and אבישי saves him with a holy שם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישבי בנוב realizes that with אבישי there, he now faces two fighters, so he tries to finish דוד off quickly. אבישי does not win by strength here. He uses a holy שם of ה׳ to stop דוד's fall in mid-air.

keyTerms.meaning: between heaven and earth, in mid-air

phrases.english: When Yishbi BeNov saw him,
he said: Now there are two of them
and they will kill me.
He threw David up high,
and stuck his spear into the ground.
He said: Let him fall on it and be killed.
Avishai said a Name,
and held David up between heaven and earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: אבישי arrives where ישבי בנוב is holding דוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבישי saves דוד from the spear by saying a holy שם that holds him in mid-air.

steps.title: Why didn't דוד say the שם himself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why דוד needed אבישי. He could have said the holy שם and saved himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let דוד himself say the שם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps out of the story to ask a question about it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד surely knew the holy שם too. If one person's saying it could save him, why did he have to wait for אבישי?

phrases.english: But let him say it himself?
phrases.notes: He means: why didn't דוד say the holy Name himself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions a detail of the rescue in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story's detail that דוד needed אבישי to say the holy שם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If saying the שם works, דוד could have said it himself, so אבישי's role seems unneeded.

steps.title: A prisoner cannot free himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a saying: a prisoner cannot release himself from prison. Someone in trouble needs another person to save him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A prisoner does not free himself from prison.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a well-known rule: someone who is trapped cannot free himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד was the one in danger, so he could not be his own rescuer. Freeing him had to come from outside, through אבישי.
steps.whatToRemember: אבישי had to save דוד because a person in trouble cannot free himself: אין חבוש מוציא עצמו מבית האסורין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saying is used in other places too, to teach that a person in trouble needs someone else to help him out.

phrases.english: A prisoner does not release himself
from the prison.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין חָבוּשׁ מוֹצִיא עַצְמוֹ מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דוד could have said the שם and saved himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: A person who is trapped cannot free himself. He needs someone else, so אבישי had to say the שם.

steps.title: אבישי tells דוד to reverse his prayer
steps.stepSummary: אבישי asks דוד why he is in danger. דוד explains the deal he made with הקב״ה. אבישי tells him to change his prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבישי said to דוד: What are you doing here? דוד said: This is what הקב״ה said to me, and this is what I answered Him. אבישי said: Reverse your prayer! Better that your grandson be a poor wax-seller than that you yourself suffer.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. אבישי asks דוד how he got into this trouble, and then tells him to change the choice he made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד explains that he is suffering because of a choice he made with הקב״ה. אבישי pushes back with a popular saying: better that your descendants live poorly than that you suffer now. This opens the door for דוד to ask for a different outcome.

phrases.english: He said to him: What are you doing here?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אֲמַר לִי קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to me,
and this is what I answered Him.
He said to him: Reverse your prayer!
Let your son's son sell wax,
phrases.notes: A popular saying: let your grandson be a poor peddler.

phrases.english: and you will not suffer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the rescue story right after the גמרא explained why דוד needed אבישי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבישי tells דוד to change his prayer, so that he himself will not suffer.

steps.title: דוד asks אבישי for help, matching the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: דוד agrees and asks אבישי to help him. The גמרא links this to the פסוק that says אבישי helped him.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד said: If so, help me. That is what the פסוק means: 'And אבישי בן צרויה helped him.'
steps.whatsHappening: דוד accepts אבישי's advice and asks for help. The גמרא shows that the פסוק describes exactly this moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אבישי helped him' in the פסוק now get a backstory: דוד asked for help after agreeing to change his prayer. The next step will explain what kind of help it was.

keyTerms.meaning: That is what is written; this explains the verse

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הָכִי, סַיַּיע בַּהֲדַן.
phrases.english: He said to him: If so, help me.
That is what is written:
"And Abishai son of Zeruiah helped him."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 21:17

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הָכִי, סַיַּיע בַּהֲדַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: דוד responds to אבישי's advice, and the גמרא ties it to a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק 'ויעזר לו אבישי' describes דוד asking אבישי for help.

steps.title: אבישי helped through prayer and brought דוד down
steps.stepSummary: רב says the help was prayer. אבישי said a holy שם and brought דוד safely down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: He helped him with prayer. אבישי said a holy שם and brought דוד down.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains what kind of help the פסוק means: אבישי helped דוד by praying. Then אבישי uses a holy שם to bring דוד down to the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says 'he helped him.' רב tells us the help was spiritual (prayer), not just physical. Earlier, אבישי's holy שם held דוד in the air. Now a second שם lands him safely.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
That he helped him with prayer.
Abishai said a holy name and brought him down.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: שֶׁעֲזָרוֹ בִּתְפִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word 'helped' in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבישי's help was prayer. He said a holy שם and brought דוד down.

steps.title: The chase and the killing of ישבי בנוב
steps.stepSummary: ישבי בנוב chases דוד and אבישי. They gain courage along the way, and they kill him after mentioning his dead mother ערפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ישבי בנוב chased after them. When they reached קובי, they said: Stand up against him. When they reached בי תרי, they said: Two cubs killed the lion. They told him: Go find ערפה your mother in the grave. When they mentioned his mother's name, his strength weakened and they killed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. ישבי בנוב chases them, they take courage from the names of the places they pass, and they kill him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each place name is read as a hint. 'קובי' sounds like 'קום ביה' (stand up against him), and 'בי תרי' sounds like 'בתרי' (with two). Earlier אבישי killed ערפה (step 25). Hearing that his mother was dead broke ישבי בנוב's strength.

phrases.english: He was chasing after them.
phrases.notes: 'He' is ישבי בנוב.

phrases.english: When they reached Kuvi,
they said: Stand up against him.
phrases.notes: A play on the place name: קובי sounds like 'קום ביה.'

phrases.english: When they reached Bei Terei,
they said: With two cubs they killed the lion.
They said to him: Go and find
Orpah your mother in the grave.
phrases.notes: אבישי had killed her on the way (step 25).

phrases.english: When they mentioned his mother's name to him,
his strength weakened and they killed him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After דוד lands, the story moves to the chase and the end of ישבי בנוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד and אבישי killed ישבי בנוב after weakening him by mentioning his dead mother.

steps.title: דוד's men swear he will not go to war again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ties the end of the story to the פסוק where דוד's men swear he will not fight with them anymore.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is what is written: 'Then דוד's men swore to him, saying: You will not go out with us to war anymore, and you will not put out the lamp of ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story closes with a פסוק. After this close call, דוד's men make him promise to stop going out to battle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole story explains why this oath happened. דוד nearly died, so his men called him 'the lamp of Israel' and would not let him risk his life in war again.

keyTerms.meaning: The lamp of Israel (דוד the king)

steps.whatToRemember: The story of ישבי בנוב explains the פסוק in שמואל ב: דוד nearly died, אבישי saved him through prayer and a holy שם, and afterward דוד's men swore he would not go out to war again.

phrases.english: That is what is written:
"Then David's men swore to him, saying:
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 21:17

phrases.english: You will not go out with us to war anymore,
and you will not put out the lamp of Israel."

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב: אָז נִשְׁבְּעוּ אַנְשֵׁי דָוִד לוֹ לֵאמֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story by linking its ending to the פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: After almost losing דוד, his men swore he would never go out to battle with them again.

steps.title: Three people for whom the land shrank
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three people who had a miracle of קפיצת הדרך: אליעזר, יעקב אבינו and אבישי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: For three people the land shrank: אליעזר עבד אברהם, יעקב אבינו, and אבישי בן צרויה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא connected to the story, since אבישי's land shrank on his way to דוד. It lists three people who had this miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, sparked by the detail in step 25 that the land shrank for אבישי. The ברייתא names the three people. The next step will show where each one comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The land jumped (shrank) for them; a miraculous short trip

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
For three people the land jumped —
phrases.notes: 'Jumped' means the trip became miraculously short, so they arrived very fast.

phrases.english: Eliezer the servant of Abraham, and Jacob our father,
and Abishai son of Zeruiah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה קָפְצָה לָהֶם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related topic, prompted by the miracle that happened to אבישי in the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three people had קפיצת הדרך: אליעזר, יעקב אבינו and אבישי.

steps.title: Sources for אבישי and אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains each name. אבישי is the story we just told. אליעזר comes from a פסוק showing he arrived the same day he left. Then the גמרא begins יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבישי בן צרויה — that is what we just said. אליעזר עבד אברהם — as it is written: 'And I came today to the spring.' This means he left that same day. יעקב אבינו —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through the list and shows where we know each case from. It finishes אבישי and אליעזר, and starts to explain יעקב (his explanation continues on the next amud).
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אבישי, the source is the story already told. For אליעזר, the word 'היום' (today) in his report shows he left and arrived on the same day, which could only happen by a miracle. The line about יעקב is a setup: his source comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: That is to say; this shows

phrases.english: Abishai son of Zeruiah — that is what we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to the story, where the land shrank for him on his way to דוד.

phrases.english: Eliezer the servant of Abraham — as it is written:
"And I came today to the spring,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 24:42

phrases.english: which is to say that he left on that same day.
Jacob our father —
phrases.notes: The explanation for יעקב continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the sources for the names listed in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבישי's miracle is from the story. אליעזר's comes from 'ואבא היום,' which shows he arrived the same day he left.
